explanation.paragraph: `src/shaders/arrow.wgsl` generates `18` shaft and start/end head vertices per vector by accepting scalar/vector arguments individually rather than a packed `VectorRow` struct, avoiding an observed Android WebGPU driver struct-argument corruption bug.

explanation.paragraph: Emits one oversized `3`-vertex fullscreen triangle with `0` primitive ID so background pixels never occlude ink as triangles.

explanation.paragraph: `src/shaders/clip.wgsl` declares up to `6` world/screen section planes with scale-aware face slack, ink dot-product tolerance, self-exemption for plane widgets and `CLIPPING` specialization.

explanation.heading: ### Compare ink with the right surface
explanation.paragraph: Derives fractional sample coverage and exact per-sample masks from nonzero primitive IDs so `4×` MSAA silhouettes stay razor-sharp.

explanation.heading: ### Draw dots and vertex markers
explanation.paragraph: Expands `3`-vertex screen-space triangles around dots, preserving a `0.5 px` minimum anti-aliased disc and distinct marker/point-query pick IDs.

explanation.heading: ### Pass order and visibility
explanation.paragraph: Generates `11 + 11` construction-plane lines (`1,000`-unit spacing across `±5,000`) plus RGB axes directly from `@builtin(vertex_index)`.

explanation.heading: ### Compare ink with the right surface
explanation.paragraph: Tests stroke fragments against `1×`/`4×` depth, primitive IDs and the pixel's tile triangle list, accounting for local depth slope and curved-chord facet sag.

explanation.paragraph: `src/shaders/normals.wgsl` transforms normals by cofactor inverse-transpose (preserving reflection sign) and decodes octahedral unit vectors while reserving `0x80008000` for absent normals.

explanation.paragraph: `src/shaders/physical.wgsl` splits `32`-bit triangle IDs across two `16`-bit halves alongside colour and `(object, subobject)` pick outputs so `4×` MSAA targets stay compatible.

explanation.paragraph: `src/shaders/surface_outline.wgsl` composites crisp silhouettes and selection outlines from a bounded pixel-offset ring without confusing object IDs with alpha coverage.
